# How Do I Switch Between Dark and Light Mode for Daily Use Comfort?


You switch between dark and light mode through a simple display setting, letting each person choose what's most comfortable for their own daily use, whether in bright daylight or a dim room. On **Jestor** , this runs through native **Dark Mode** support.


Working in a bright interface during a late night session, or a dark interface in bright daylight, creates unnecessary eye strain that a simple display toggle would eliminate.


## What a single fixed display mode costs


- Eye strain from working in a bright interface during low-light conditions
- Reduced visibility from a dark interface in bright ambient light
- No personal choice for what's genuinely comfortable for each individual
- Discomfort accumulating over long working sessions without a mode that fits


## How dark and light mode switching works


- A simple toggle switches between **dark mode** and standard light mode
- This applies consistently across tables, apps, and documents
- Each person can choose the mode that suits their own working conditions
- The switch takes effect immediately, without disrupting the actual work


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- The toggle gives each person control over their own visual comfort
- Consistent application across tables, apps, and documents avoids a jarring mix
- This reduces eye strain during long sessions in varying light conditions
- This scales from an individual preference to a team where everyone chooses their own mode


Single fixed display mode Toggleable dark and light mode


Doesn't fit every condition Chosen per individual comfort


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does dark mode apply to documents as well as tables and apps?** Yes, dark mode support extends to documents too. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Is this setting personal, or does it apply to the whole team?** It's typically a personal display preference for each individual user.


**Does switching modes affect any of the underlying data or functionality?** No, it's purely a visual display setting.
